first_line_treatment.indication: First-line for ALL type 2 diabetes (NICE NG28, 2024 update)
first_line_treatment.notes: SGLT2i now recommended alongside metformin from the start, not as add-on

first_line_treatment.indication: Metformin intolerance or eGFR <30 contraindicating metformin

atherosclerotic_CVD.treatment: Metformin + SGLT2i + Semaglutide (Ozempic) up to 1mg weekly

CKD_eGFR_below_20.treatment: DPP-4 inhibitor; alternatives: pioglitazone or insulin

early_onset.treatment: Metformin + SGLT2i, then consider GLP-1 RA or Tirzepatide

frailty.treatment: Metformin only; DPP-4 inhibitor if metformin unsuitable

second_line_treatment.drug_class: Add GLP-1 receptor agonist or DPP-4 inhibitor or Sulfonylurea

options.notes: Risk of hypoglycaemia and weight gain
Avoid in heart failure or bladder cancer risk

second_line_treatment.indication: HbA1c not at target on metformin + SGLT2i

options: Metformin + insulin (usually basal insulin — NPH or Glargine/Detemir)
third_line_treatment.indication: HbA1c not at target on dual therapy

insulin_regimens.notes: Start 10 units at bedtime, titrate by 2 units every 3 days to fasting glucose target

examples: Basal + rapid-acting insulin (Novorapid, Humalog) before meals

insulin_regimens.notes: Alternative to basal-bolus if simpler regimen preferred

hba1c_targets.on_drugs_causing_hypos: 53 mmol/mol (7.0%) — if on sulfonylurea or insulin
hba1c_targets.individualised: Adjust for frailty, life expectancy, hypoglycaemia risk

contraindicated_drugs.drug: SGLT2 inhibitor if recurrent UTI/DKA risk

monitoring: HbA1c: every 3-6 months until stable, then 6-monthly
non_pharmacological: Dietary advice: low glycaemic index, reduce refined carbs
